extension.title: Copilot Scheduler
config.showNotifications: Show notifications when tasks are executed
config.executionHistoryLimit: Number of recent execution history entries to keep per task (10–500)
config.language: UI language (applies to extension Webview/Tree UI; settings-description updates may require window reload)
config.timezone: Timezone for cron scheduling, the allowed time window and the daily execution counters (e.g., 'Asia/Tokyo'). Leave empty for system default.
config.chatSession: Default chat session behavior. Tasks can override this.
config.chatSession.new: Create new chat session for each execution (more isolated, usually slower)
config.chatSession.continue: Continue in existing chat session (usually faster)
config.skillTemplates: Which Agent Skills the task form offers to insert into a prompt as `/skill-name`. Skills are read from `.github/skills`, `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` in local workspace folders (trusted workspaces only) and from `~/.copilot/skills` (or `$COPILOT_HOME/skills`), `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.claude/skills`. A skill is listed only when its folder name, `name`, and the Agent Skills naming rules agree. A workspace skill hides a user skill with the same name; a name found twice at the same level is left out. Skills with `user-invocable: false` are never listed. The form has Local Skill and Global Skill options that list workspace skills and user skills respectively, and a toggle to show all skills.
config.skillTemplates.explicit: Only skills that run when invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`) (default)
config.skillTemplates.off: Do not offer skills in the task form
config.sessionHarness: Which kind of chat session new runs start in. Applies only when a run starts a new chat session. `auto` leaves the choice to VS Code. `local` is experimental: it starts a Local chat session with the `workbench.action.chat.newLocalChat` command and does not send the task if that fails. Scheduler never changes your VS Code settings and cannot force a Copilot (Agent Host) session.
config.sessionHarness.auto: Use the session type VS Code chooses for new chats (default)
config.sessionHarness.local: Experimental: start a Local chat session for each new run
config.executionRoute: How a task is run. `agentHost` (default) sends the selected model ID and supported options to VS Code's Agent Host. A matching reported ID does not independently verify the backend. `chat` uses the older Copilot Chat route. A recurring task's Copilot CLI option takes priority. With `sessionHarness` set to `local`, or in a remote window, recurring tasks use chat. One-time tasks require Agent Host and do not run through chat or CLI.
config.executionRoute.chat: Run through a Copilot Chat session (older route)
config.executionFallback: What to do when a recurring task cannot run through the Agent Host before dispatch. `chat` allows the chat route and records why; model application is unverified. `fail`, a task's route guard, or an existing-chat binding stops instead. One-time tasks require Agent Host. Dispatched or uncertain runs are never automatically resent.
config.executionFallback.fail: Do not run; show a warning
config.agentHostAutoApprove: Let tasks run through the Agent Host use tools without asking for approval. On by default: an unattended task cannot answer an approval prompt, so without this a task that edits files or runs commands would not complete. Turn it off only if you accept that such tasks may be refused. Only a user or remote setting is honored.
config.agentHostOpenSession: Open the session of a task run through the Agent Host as an editor tab once the run has started, so you can watch it. On by default. Turn it off for frequent unattended tasks that should not bring a tab to the front; the session still appears in the session list.
config.agentHostTimeoutEnabled: Cancel an Agent Host run that takes longer than `#copilotScheduler.agentHostTimeoutMinutes#`. Off by default, so a long run is never cancelled. A run stuck waiting for input or authentication then stays running until you act; later occurrences of a recurring task still start unless its overlap option is off. If you set the minutes before this option existed and have not set this option, the timeout stays on. Only a user or remote setting is honored.
config.agentHostTimeoutMinutes: Minutes before an Agent Host run is cancelled when `#copilotScheduler.agentHostTimeoutEnabled#` is on (default 180). If cancellation cannot be confirmed, the outcome is unknown and the run may continue. Only a user or remote setting is honored.
config.cliPath: Full path of the `copilot` executable used by tasks that run with the Copilot CLI. Leave empty to find `copilot` (`copilot.exe` on Windows) on PATH. Only a user or remote setting is honored, never a workspace setting.
config.cliAllowAllTools: Let a task that runs with the Copilot CLI use every tool without asking (`--allow-all-tools`). Off by default: the CLI cannot ask for approval in a background run, so tools are then refused and a task that needs to edit files or run commands will not complete. Turn it on only if you accept that unattended tasks can run commands and change files in the task's folder. Only a user or remote setting is honored.
config.cliTimeoutEnabled: Stop a Copilot CLI run that takes longer than `#copilotScheduler.cliTimeoutMinutes#`. Off by default, so a long run is never stopped; a manual run then waits until the CLI exits. If you set the minutes before this option existed and have not set this option, the timeout stays on. Only a user or remote setting is honored.
config.cliTimeoutMinutes: Minutes after which a task that runs with the Copilot CLI is stopped when `#copilotScheduler.cliTimeoutEnabled#` is on (1-720, default 180). Only a user or remote setting is honored.
config.showCopilotCliControls: Show the Copilot CLI route control in Advanced in the task editor. This only changes visibility, not saved tasks or execution. Changes apply immediately.
config.modelFallbackChain: Legacy fallback order retained for compatibility with older versions. Tasks in the current task editor use their own replacement models and priority instead.
config.autoModeDefault: Default value for new tasks' auto-mode hint (inserts an autonomous-execution instruction at the beginning of the runtime prompt). To automatically keep AI-applied edits, configure `#chat.editing.autoAcceptDelay#`. If the link does not open, search for chat.editing.autoAcceptDelay in Settings.
config.commandDelayFactor: Delay multiplier for Copilot command sequencing (0.1–2.0). Lower is faster but may reduce stability in some environments.
config.manualRunNextRunPolicy: How to compute next run after Run Now
config.manualRunNextRunPolicy.advance: Advance past an existing future next run; otherwise recalculate from the current time
config.manualRunNextRunPolicy.fromNow: Recalculate from current time (ignores existing future next run)
config.missedRunPolicy: How to handle tasks due before scheduler start or restart. Evaluated on the next scheduler check; tasks due after startup are unaffected.
config.missedRunPolicy.runOnce: Run each overdue task once, regardless of how many occurrences were missed
config.missedRunPolicy.skip: Skip overdue tasks without recording an execution; advance each schedule to its next future occurrence
config.jitterSeconds: Default max random delay in seconds before running a task (0 = off). Each task can override this.
config.maxDailyExecutions: Maximum scheduled executions per day across all tasks (0 = unlimited, 1–100). ⚠️ Unlimited may risk API rate-limiting.
config.minimumIntervalWarning: Show a warning when a cron interval is shorter than 30 minutes
config.globalPromptsPath: Custom path for global prompt templates. Default: VS Code's User/prompts folder (Windows: %APPDATA%/Code/User/prompts, macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/prompts, Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Code/User/prompts or ~/.config/Code/User/prompts)
config.globalAgentsPath: Custom path for global agent files (*.agent.md). Default: auto-detect VS Code's User/prompts folder plus ~/.copilot/agents (Windows: %USERPROFILE%/.copilot/agents). Setting this overrides the default discovery roots.
config.promptFileFallback: What to do when a task using a local or global prompt file cannot read that file at execution time. Inline prompts are never affected.
config.promptFileFallback.snapshot: Run the saved prompt snapshot (current behavior).
config.promptFileFallback.blockWhenResol: Block the run when the prompt file path resolves but the file cannot be read. Fall back to the snapshot when the path cannot be resolved at all (for example the workspace is not open).
config.promptFileFallback.blockAlways: Block the run whenever the latest prompt file cannot be read.
config.reportIssue: 🐛 Found a bug? [Report an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/aktsmm/vscode-copilot-scheduler/issues)
config.lmTools.enableWriteTools: Allow Copilot Chat / agent mode to create, update, delete, toggle and run scheduler tasks via language-model tools. When disabled, write tools remain visible but their invocations are blocked; read tools remain usable.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode: Controls the extension-provided custom confirmation messages for Copilot Chat language-model write tools. VS Code or Copilot Chat may still show a generic approval dialog.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode.always: Always show custom confirmation messages from the extension for create, update, delete, enable-disable, and run tools.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode.destruct: Show custom confirmation messages from the extension only for destructive operations such as delete.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode.minimal: Suppress all extension-provided custom confirmation messages. VS Code or Copilot Chat may still show generic approval.
tool.scheduler_manage.modelDescription: Use when the user asks to create, edit, delete, run, enable, or disable a scheduled Copilot task. First use scheduler_query to identify an existing task. Set action=create with task, update with id and updates, delete or run with id, or enable with id and a boolean enabled. Update cannot change enabled; enabling requires first-run consent. For recurring prompts, prefer an explicit-only skill (disable-model-invocation: true) invoked as /skill-name; create and update report limited skill discovery. Model and agent IDs must be selected from scheduler_query catalogs, never guessed; use list_sessions before selecting targetChatId. For agentHostModelId use the exact ID from list_agent_host_models. The catalog does not verify correspondence with model; if unclear, ask the user to select the matching ID. Run bypasses jitter, time windows and daily limits; success means dispatch, not completed work. Never automatically retry a dispatched, queued, failed, cancelled or uncertain run; inspect history. One-time runs are reserved and disabled first, and afterRun deletion follows success and saved history. The same saved tool approval can apply to every action, including delete and run.
tool.scheduler_query.modelDescription: Query Copilot Scheduler for task information without side effects. Set 'kind' to one of: 'list' (tasks without prompt bodies), 'get' (one task including its prompt), 'history', 'preview_cron', 'list_models', 'list_agent_host_models' (exact live Agent Host IDs and names), 'list_agents', 'list_skills', or 'list_sessions' (existing Copilot chats with opaque bindingId values; chat content and internal URIs are omitted). Always use this before making changes to confirm which task the user means. Call 'list_sessions' before binding a task to an existing chat; never guess a bindingId. Call 'list_models' / 'list_agents' / 'list_skills' before choosing those values. For agentHostModelId, use an exact ID selected from 'list_agent_host_models'; never infer or guess it. Never write promptPreview back to a task; fetch the full prompt with 'get' first.
